title: A set of acyclic monomorphisms detects dg injectivity
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebra. Use left sheaf dg modules and signed homogeneous maps as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. For dg modules $M,I$ let $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^{\bullet}(M,I)$ be the complex of global homogeneous $\mathcal A$-linear sheaf maps, with differential $\delta(h)=d_Ih-(-1)^{|h|}hd_M$. Call $I$ homotopically injective if this complex is acyclic for every $M$ with all underlying cohomology sheaves zero. Call $I$ graded injective if its underlying graded $\mathcal A$-module is injective: every degree-zero graded module map from a graded submodule $N\subseteq N'$ to $I$ extends to $N'$. There is a set $R$ of monomorphisms $a_r:E_r\hookrightarrow F_r$ of acyclic sheaf dg $\mathcal A$-modules such that, for every dg module $I$, the following are equivalent: (i) $I$ is graded injective and homotopically injective; (ii) for every $r\in R$ and every degree-zero dg module map $u:E_r\to I$ there is a degree-zero dg module map $v:F_r\to I$ with $v a_r=u$.

source.place: Tag 0FSY (lemma-better-set-of-monos); K-injective means the global Hom-complex condition of definition-K-injective, with all shifts. Left modules by the graded opposite algebra.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-graded-sheaf-module-grothendieck], choose a generator $U$ of $\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$. Take a set of representatives $b_t:B_t\hookrightarrow U$ of its graded subobjects (these form a set: each is specified by subsheaves of the component sheaves on the set of opens). By [lem-pur-kinjective-characterize-injective], a graded module is injective exactly when maps from every $B_t$ extend to $U$. Use the adjunction of [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-acyclic-hull]. It gives acyclic monomorphisms $G(b_t):G(B_t)\hookrightarrow G(U)$, and naturality identifies their extension conditions with those for $b_t$. Thus these tests detect graded injectivity.

Choose $\{N_s\}_{s\in S}$ from [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-small-acyclic-subobjects]. For every $s$ and $k\in\mathbf Z$, add the inclusion $j_{s,k}:L=N_s[k]\hookrightarrow C(1_L)=L\oplus L[1]$, $l\mapsto(l,0)$, to the tests of step 1. These form a set $R=T\amalg(S\times\mathbf Z)$. With the signed action and differential of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization], the degree $-1$ map $s(x,y)=(0,x)$ satisfies $d s+s d=1$ and $s(a(x,y))=(-1)^{|a|}a s(x,y)$. Hence the cone is contractible and acyclic; its source is acyclic too.

source.place: Tag 0FSY (lemma-better-set-of-monos), construction of R; cone calculation written out in the stated left-module convention

proof.text: Assume (i). For any test $a:E\hookrightarrow F$ and dg map $u:E\to I$, acyclicity of $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal A}(E,I)$ supplies a signed graded map $h$ of degree $-1$ with $\delta h=u$. Graded injectivity also extends maps of degree $q$: such maps are degree-zero maps into the graded module underlying $I[q]$, which is injective because the signed shift is an equivalence with inverse shift $[-q]$. Extend $h$ to $h\prime:F\to I$. Then $v=\delta h\prime$ is a dg map since $\delta^2=0$, and $va=\delta(h\prime a)=\delta h=u$. This proves (ii).

Conversely assume (ii). Step 1 gives graded injectivity. For each $s,k$, every dg map $u:N_s[k]\to I$ extends to its cone by step 2. If $v$ is the extension, then $v s j_{s,k}$ is a degree $-1$ null homotopy of $u$, since $\delta(vs j_{s,k})=v j_{s,k}=u$. A degree $q$ cocycle $z:N_s\to I$ is exactly a dg map $N_s[-q]\to I$ after reindexing. A degree $-1$ null homotopy for that map is a degree $q-1$ map $h$ with $z=d_Ih+(-1)^q h d_{N_s}=\delta h$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal A}(N_s,I)$ is acyclic in every degree.

source.place: Tag 0FSY (lemma-better-set-of-monos), converse, vanishing on the small acyclics and all their shifts

proof.text: For later use, if $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ is an exact sequence of dg modules, then $0\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(C,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(A,I)\to0$ is exact as a sequence of complexes of abelian groups. Indeed degree-$q$ surjectivity is graded injectivity applied to $I[q]$; a homogeneous map vanishing on $A$ factors uniquely through the graded quotient $C$. Restriction commutes with $\delta$ by its displayed formula. This argument uses graded injectivity from step 4, and does not assert that the terms of the underlying $\mathcal O$-complex of $I$ are injective.

source.place: Tag 0FSQ (remark-why-graded-injective), direct proof of the degreewise exact Hom sequence

proof.text: Let $M$ be any acyclic dg module. Build acyclic submodules $K_\alpha\subseteq M$ by transfinite recursion, with $K_0=0$. If $K_\beta\ne M$, the quotient $M/K_\beta$ is nonzero and acyclic by [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-grothendieck] and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-small-acyclic-subobjects] to embed some nonzero $N_s$ in that quotient; let $K_{\beta+1}$ be its inverse image. Then $K_{\beta+1}/K_\beta\cong N_s$ and $K_{\beta+1}$ is acyclic by the same long exact sequence. If $K_\beta=M$, keep it unchanged. At a limit take the filtered colimit, which is still a submodule of $M$ and acyclic by the colimit and cohomology clauses of [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-grothendieck]. Before reaching $M$ every successor strictly increases. Submodules of $M$ form a set (degreewise subsheaves on a set of opens), so this recursion must reach $M$ before the successor cardinal of that set.

Prove by transfinite induction that $H_\alpha=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal A}(K_\alpha,I)$ is acyclic. At zero this is immediate. At a nonconstant successor, step 5 gives $0\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(N_s,I)\to H_{\beta+1}\to H_\beta\to0$. Its first term is acyclic by step 4 and its last by induction, so its middle term is acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. The constant successor changes nothing.

source.place: Tag 0FSY (lemma-better-set-of-monos), successor Hom-vanishing argument; correct contravariant order

proof.text: At a limit $\lambda$, the degreewise colimit statement of [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-grothendieck] and the universal property of a colimit give $H_\lambda=\varprojlim_{\beta<\lambda}H_\beta$, including the differentials and signed actions. For every $\beta<\lambda$, the map $H_\beta^q\to\varprojlim_{\gamma<\beta}H_\gamma^q$ is surjective: if $\beta=\gamma+1$ this is restriction to $K_\gamma$, which is surjective by graded injectivity as in step 5; if $\beta$ is a nonzero limit it is an isomorphism by continuity of $K$; if $\beta=0$ the target is zero. All earlier $H_\beta$ are acyclic by induction. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-ML-ordinals] to deduce acyclicity of $H_\lambda$. At the stage where $K_\alpha=M$, this says that $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal A}(M,I)$ is acyclic. As $M$ was arbitrary, (i) follows.
